title_ar: الشيخ  محمد الحسن الددو يلقي محاضرة في جامعة انواكشوط بعنوان:"عظمة الله تعالى"
title_en: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew Delivers a Lecture at the University of Nouakchott Entitled "The Greatness of God Most High"
body_ar: ألقى فضيلة العلامة الشيخ محمد الحسن الددو رئيس مركز تكوين العلماء في مدرج المعرفة بجامعة انواكشوط محاضرة بعنوان: "عظمة الله سبحانه وتعالى"، كانت محاضرة رائعة بكل المقاييس جسدت بحق شعار الأسبوع الثقافي: "تعظيم الحرمات"، الذي يقيمه الناديان الجامعيان؛ نادي الرأي الثقافي ونادي صناع الحياة. تطرق الشيخ – حفظه الله – في هذه المحاضرة لمظاهر عظمة الله تعالى من خلال التدبر والتفكر في آيات الله المسطورة والمنظورة وتعظيم الحرمات، ونجمل ما تعرض له الشيخ فيما يلي: • -أن أسماء الله الحسنى وصفاته العلا وكلامه متى شاء وكيف شاء وأمره الذي بين الكاف والنون ... كل هذا يدل على عظمة الله سبحانه تعالى. • -أن من عجائب التشريع التي تجسد عظمة الله سبحانه وتعالى كون القرآن الكريم كتاب محفوظ محيط بكل أحكام هذه الحياة؛ الخير كله فيما أمر به، و الشر كله فيما نهى عنه، لا يصح الاستغناء عن شيء منه، حتى الحدود التي هي زواجر وجوابر فيها فوائد عظيمة، لا يسد مسدها أي تشريع آخر. • -أن من التشريع ما هو تعبدي ومنه ما هو تعللي - حسب الأصوليين -؛ فالتعبدي ما كانت مصلحته الغالبة أخروية وقد تكون فيه مصالح دنيوية، والتعللي ما ظهرت حكمته الدنيوية، وقد تكون فيه مصالح أخروية. • -أن للقرآن الكريم في القصص وعرض آيات الله المسطورة والمنظورة في الكون، أسلوب عجيب يستوقف أصحاب الذوق الرفيع في البلاغة.
body_en:
His eminence the erudite Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan al-Dedew, head of the Centre for the Formation of Scholars, delivered a lecture in the Knowledge Lecture Hall at the University of Nouakchott entitled "The Greatness of God, glorified and exalted is He". It was a splendid lecture by every measure, and it truly embodied the theme of the cultural week, "Honouring the Sanctities", which is being held by the two university clubs: the Cultural Opinion Club and the Makers of Life Club. The Sheikh — may God preserve him — dealt in this lecture with the manifestations of the greatness of God Most High, by way of pondering and reflecting upon God's signs, both those written down and those seen, and upon the honouring of the sanctities. We summarise what the Sheikh treated as follows:

• That God's most beautiful names, His most exalted attributes, His speech whenever He wills and however He wills, and His command which lies between the kāf and the nūn ... all of this indicates the greatness of God, glorified and exalted.

• That among the wonders of the legislation which embody the greatness of God, glorified and exalted is He, is that the Noble Qur'an is a preserved book encompassing all the rulings of this life: all good lies in what it has commanded, and all evil in what it has forbidden. It is not sound to dispense with any part of it — even the prescribed punishments (ḥudūd), which are both deterrent and restorative, contain immense benefits, and no other legislation can take their place.

• That some of the legislation is devotional and some of it is cause-based — according to the legal theorists (uṣūliyyūn). The devotional is that whose predominant benefit is otherworldly, though there may be worldly benefits within it; and the cause-based is that whose worldly wisdom is apparent, though there may be otherworldly benefits within it.

• That the Noble Qur'an has, in its narratives and in its setting out of God's signs both written down and seen in the cosmos, a wondrous manner which arrests those of refined taste in eloquence.

flags.arabic: أن من التشريع ما هو تعبدي ومنه ما هو تعللي - حسب الأصوليين -
flags.context: the distinction drawn in the third summarised point
options: devotional (taʿabbudī) and cause-based (taʿallulī), as the terms stand
read 'تعللي' as the more usual 'معلل' (whose operative cause is stated) and translate accordingly
flags.note: The standard pair in legal theory is taʿabbudī against maʿqūl al-maʿnā or muʿallal; 'تعللي' is an unusual formation and may be the summariser's word rather than the Sheikh's. Neither term is in the glossary. The English renders the pair transparently and does not substitute the more usual term, because the point turns on a definition the summary itself supplies in the next clause. Worth settling corpus-wide, since the distinction recurs.

options: render the allusion literally and keep the source's own ellipsis
expand it to 'His command "Be", and it is'
flags.note: 'Between the kāf and the nūn' alludes to the divine command kun, 'Be'. Rendered literally, with the allusion left to work as it does in the Arabic, and the source's own trailing ellipsis preserved — the ellipsis is the summariser's mark of omission, and text may be missing at that point.

flags.arabic: حتى الحدود التي هي زواجر وجوابر
flags.context: the aside on the prescribed punishments within the second point
flags.note: 'zawājir wa-jawābir' is a fixed technical pair: a ḥadd both deters the offence and repairs or expiates what has been done. The English keeps both limbs, since dropping the second would make the sentence purely punitive. Editorially sensitive in that a summary sentence affirming the ḥudūd will be quoted on its own; note that it is one clause of a lecture on the divine attributes, is second-hand, and carries no ruling on the application of any punishment.

flags.arabic: نجمل ما تعرض له الشيخ فيما يلي
flags.context: the framing of the summarised points
options: keep the reporting frame visible and never present the points as the Sheikh's own words
present the points as direct statements by the Sheikh
flags.note: The site editor states that the points are his own summary of a spoken lecture, not a transcript. Every proposition is therefore second-hand and must not be quoted as the Sheikh's written words.

translator_notes: A site news summary of a lecture, not a text by the Sheikh; the reporting frame is preserved throughout.
The praise of the lecture ('splendid by every measure') is the site editor's, and the English keeps it plainly as his.
'آيات الله المسطورة والمنظورة' is the classical pairing of the revealed signs and the signs in creation; rendered as 'written down' and 'seen' so that the pairing survives.

The page ends with a navigation line inviting the reader to click through to the recording in the site's separate media system; it is a site affordance rather than content and is not part of body_ar or body_en.
